title: Annotatio V §.XI: Forbes/Fabricius — Calvin with Irenaeus on spiritual not corporal/local presence
pass_a_gloss: Although that Calvin most amicably conspires with Irenaeus as to the matter, William Forbes the Reformed and Johannes Fabricius the Lutheran most fully prove; and what appears published contrary by Calvin is easily reconciled by the Distinction between Spiritual presence of Christ’s body in the Supper and Corporal or Local — of which Calvin admits the former with Irenaeus, rejects the latter with all Antiquity, having with the same most constantly professed that Christ’s body in a corporal and local mode is only in heaven, not in the Supper or everywhere.
pass_b_english: Forbes (Reformed) and Fabricius (Lutheran) show Calvin agrees with Irenaeus on the matter.

Apparent clashes resolve by spiritual vs corporal/local presence: Calvin with Irenaeus keeps the spiritual; with all antiquity he rejects corporal/local presence in the Supper or everywhere — body only in heaven that way.
source_text: Quanquam Calvinum quà rem cum Irenæo amicissimè conspirare fusissimè evincunt Guilielmus Forbes. Reformatus, & Johannes Fabricius, Lutheranus; Quæ autem in contrarium à Calvino edita apparent, facile conciliantur Distinctione inter Præsentiam corporis Christi in Cœna Spiritualem, & Corporalem seu Localem, quarum priorem cum Irenæo admittit Calvinus, posteriorem, cum universa Antiquitate, rejicit, cum eadem constantissimè professus, corpus Christi corporali localíque modo tantùm in cælo, non autem vel in Cœna, vel ubique esse.

lemmas.gloss: Spiritual … and Corporal or Local presence
